$comment: Expected database security posture. `npm run security:check-db` diffs the LIVE
database against this file and fails on any deviation.
This file exists because of security audit finding C2: a REVOKE applied in
July 2026 silently undid itself when a function changed signature (Supabase's
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES re-grants EXECUTE to anon/authenticated on every new
function object in `public`). The hole was open for four months and nothing
detected it. Any change to this file must be a deliberate, reviewed decision.
Adding a name to allowedAnonExecute means: 'an unauthenticated caller on the
public internet may run this'. Treat such a change as a security review.
$allowedExecuteNote: Both lists are intentionally empty. Every business RPC in this codebase is
invoked exclusively by server-side code holding the service_role key:
service_role is never subject to these lists and always retains EXECUTE.
$zeroPolicyNote: otp_tokens has RLS enabled with zero policies. That is CORRECT — it is a
deliberate default-deny table reachable only by service_role. Supabase's
linter flags it at INFO level; it is not a defect.
$rlsNote: Empty by design: every table in `public` must have RLS enabled. RLS is the
entire tenant-isolation model. A new table without it is a cross-tenant leak.
